turns.speaker: Mara Ellison
turns.text: Starting a new project file with you. I'm a postdoc at Bonn working on a paper with two co-authors: Tomas Ibarra (Universidad de Santiago) and Priya Raman (University of Bristol). Working title: 'Acylindrical actions on arc-like complexes for free-by-cyclic groups'. The object of study is a complex I'm currently calling X(Gamma) built from the Bass-Serre tree of the ascending HNN extension. Theorem A gives an acylindricity constant kappa = 14 for the action of F_n rtimes_phi Z on X(Gamma) when phi is irreducible with no periodic conjugacy classes. We are aiming at Geometry & Topology, special issue.

Noted. Project frame: paper on acylindrical actions for free-by-cyclic groups, complex X(Gamma), Theorem A with kappa = 14, co-authors Tomas Ibarra (Santiago) and Priya Raman (Bristol), target Geometry & Topology special issue. I will track notation, constants, hypotheses and deadlines as they change. Two things I'd want pinned early: (1) whether acylindricity is uniform over the automorphism or only over the fixed phi, and (2) whether X(Gamma) is connected for n = 2, where the arc graph degenerates.

turns.speaker: draft-v0.3.tex
turns.text: Excerpt, draft-v0.3.tex, Section 1. THEOREM A. Let phi in Out(F_n) be irreducible with no periodic conjugacy classes, n >= 3, and let G = F_n rtimes_phi Z. Then G acts acylindrically on X(Gamma): for every epsilon > 0 there is R = R(epsilon) such that for all x, y in X(Gamma) with d(x,y) >= R, the set of g in G with d(x,gx) <= epsilon and d(y,gy) <= epsilon has cardinality at most kappa = 14. Remark 1.2: we do not know whether kappa can be taken independent of n.

turns.speaker: Mara Ellison
turns.text: A standing request about how you give me things. When you give me a proof sketch, I want it as numbered steps, one claim per step, and I want the hypotheses restated explicitly at the top of the sketch even if we just discussed them. No flowing prose paragraphs - I lose track of where a hypothesis got used, and that is exactly where my errors live.

Understood - numbered steps, hypotheses restated at the top, no prose. Sketch for Lemma 3.4 in that format. Hypotheses: H1, H subgroup of F_n; H2, phi irreducible with no periodic conjugacy classes; H3, H of finite index in F_n (as currently written in your draft). Step 1. H acts on T(Gamma) with quotient a finite graph of groups. Step 2. Pick two hyperbolic elements a, b in H with disjoint axis-endpoint pairs in partial T(Gamma). Step 3. Run a ping-pong argument on T(Gamma) with the four disjoint endpoint neighbourhoods. Step 4. Conclude a, b generate a free subgroup of rank 2 whose orbit map to X(Gamma) is a quasi-isometric embedding. Step 5. Transport the bound back to X(Gamma) using Lemma 2.7. I would run this through the Bass-Serre tree rather than directly in X(Gamma): the tree gives you honest disjointness and the complex only gives you coarse disjointness.

turns.speaker: Mara Ellison
turns.text: Counterexample. Conjecture B as stated in draft-v0.3 is false. I built a mapping torus of a pseudo-Anosov on a closed surface - I believe genus 2 - whose fundamental group is free-by-cyclic but where the orbit map to X(Gamma) has quasi-isometric constants blowing up along a sequence of powers. The dilatation is lambda = 1.83929 (largest root of x^3 - x^2 - x - 1). So the 'uniform in phi' clause in Conjecture B has to go.

That is the right shape for a counterexample to a uniformity claim. Two checks before you commit it to the draft. (1) Confirm the surface genus from the Euler characteristic of your train track, not from the picture - a genus-2 closed surface gives chi = -2 and rank 4 free group on the once-punctured version, and your stated edge count looked like chi = -4. (2) Confirm lambda = 1.83929 is the dilatation of the map and not of its square; the tribonacci value is a common off-by-one-power trap. If the genus comes out higher than 2, the blow-up rate changes and Conjecture B might survive in a weakened form restricted to the thick part.

turns.speaker: Mara Ellison
turns.text: Tomas is right that kappa = 14 is an artifact. The 14 comes from stacking a crude hyperbolicity estimate (delta = 6) on top of a bounded-diameter argument with slack. Can we do better? I don't want to lose a week on it if the answer is 'you shave off one'.

You can do better than one. Recommendation: replace the hyperbolicity argument in Lemma 3.9 with a bounded geodesic image argument in the Masur-Minsky sense, applied to the subsurface projections of the arcs rather than to the arcs themselves. Hypotheses restated: phi irreducible, no periodic conjugacy classes, n >= 3. Step 1. For each arc a, project to the annular complex of the corresponding edge of Gamma. Step 2. Bounded geodesic image gives a threshold constant C = 11 beyond which the projection is coarsely constant. Step 3. Feed C into the counting argument of Lemma 3.9 in place of the 2delta + 2 slack. Step 4. The count becomes kappa = 11 rather than 14, and the dependence on delta drops out entirely. That last point matters more than the number: your constant stops depending on an estimate you only know crudely.

turns.text: Lemma 3.4 audit. As written in draft-v0.6 the hypothesis is 'H a subgroup of finite index in F_n'. But the only place the proof uses the hypothesis is Step 3, the ping-pong, and there what I actually need is that H meets its conjugates trivially. Finite index gives me the wrong thing - a finite-index subgroup meets its conjugates in a finite-index subgroup, which is the opposite of what the argument wants. Suspect the hypothesis is simply wrong.

Your suspicion is correct and the fix is a hypothesis change, not a proof change. Hypotheses restated: phi irreducible with no periodic conjugacy classes, n >= 3, H a subgroup of F_n. Step 1. Step 3's ping-pong needs the four endpoint neighbourhoods to be genuinely disjoint, which requires H cap gHg^{-1} = 1 for g outside H - that is malnormality. Step 2. Finite index gives the reverse, so the current hypothesis does not support Step 3; worse, finite index makes the conclusion false (take H = F_n). Step 3. Replace the hypothesis with: H finitely generated and malnormal in F_n. Recommendation: state Lemma 3.4 with 'finitely generated and malnormal' and add a one-line remark that finite index is not sufficient, with H = F_n as the trivial witness.

turns.speaker: abstract-v2.txt
turns.text: Abstract, v2. We show that if phi in Out(F_n) is irreducible with no periodic conjugacy classes and n >= 3, then G = F_n rtimes_phi Z acts acylindrically on the arc-like complex A(Gamma) with acylindricity constant kappa = 11. We show further that the constant cannot be taken uniformly over all ascending HNN extensions, and we exhibit a mapping torus of a pseudo-Anosov on a closed genus-3 surface for which the orbit map degenerates along powers. As applications we obtain cyclic subgroup separability and a bound on the number of conjugacy classes of maximal cyclic subgroups.

Abstract comments. The second sentence buries the lead: say 'the constant is not uniform' before the example, since the non-uniformity is the surprising half.
